description: Universal video production rules for Generative AI. Injected automatically into all pods.

transitions.description: Choose the most appropriate transition based on pacing and narrative. Use all three types.

types.continue: Fluid static continuation. ONLY use to prolong static dialogue or a slow pan over an empty landscape. The visual_prompt MUST be exactly the same as the previous clip. If there is physical movement, pose change, or new objects, use 'cut'.
types.cut: Small cut. Change of angle/shot within the same scene. Action/dialogue continues but from another viewpoint. Main transition to be used.
types.scene_change: Large cut. Complete change of location or action. A completely new situation begins.

continue: Character is COMPLETELY STILL speaking a long phrase.
Slow pan over an empty landscape.
cut: Changing angle or shot type (e.g. medium to close-up).

transitions.golden_rule: NEVER ask a character to perform more than ONE main physical action per clip/scene. Divide actions using 'cut'. NEVER introduce a sudden scene change or new character WITHIN a single clip.
transitions.anti_morphing_rule: NEVER use 'continue' for moving actions. 'continue' will cause severe morphing if used during a pose change or camera angle change. When in doubt, ALWAYS use 'cut'.

lip_sync.description: Rules for when a character speaks.
rules: DO NOT include textual dialogues or what the character is saying inside the visual_prompt (e.g., 'The character says...' is FORBIDDEN). The visual_prompt is strictly for physical actions, environment, and emotions.
All spoken dialogue goes EXCLUSIVELY in the audio_text field.
When a character speaks, prefer 'close-up' or 'medium' shots to show their face.
No speaking off-camera unless narratively justified.
ALWAYS describe the full physical appearance of characters in every visual_prompt (clothing, colors, accessories).

ABSOLUTELY PROHIBITED to include text, subtitles, watermarks, or any written content in the visual_prompt. Always append: 'absolutely no text, no subtitles, no letters, no watermarks, no written words'.
The visual_prompt MUST be in ENGLISH.
Always prefix the visual_prompt with the art style (e.g., '3D Disney Pixar style').
DO NOT use contradictory visual concepts for an object (e.g., 'crystal acorn'). Use one clear visual identity.

prop_continuity.description: CRITICAL rules to prevent object morphing and disappearance.
rules: If a character holds an object in consecutive clips, explicitly describe it in BOTH visual_prompts using the EXACT SAME WORDS.
If an object must disappear, dedicate a short clip showing the character dropping it.
Objects cannot magically appear. Show the character grabbing it using a 'cut'.
Use consistent naming for props across all prompts (e.g., always 'small green fabric backpack').

anatomy_guard.description: Defensive rules against anatomical AI errors.
rules: Avoid complex finger or hand gestures (pointing, counting). Prefer broad actions (open arms, hand on hip).
During gestures, use medium or wide shots. Close-ups of hands cause artifacts.
Do not hold more than one object at a time.
For fluid interactions (water, mud), use wide or medium shots.

guidelines.8 seconds: Establishing scenes, emotional climax, important moments.
